question: Analyze how Raft handles non-voting members (Learners) when scaling clusters, and how it prevents network partition stalls during joint consensus membership changes.
Explain the Paxos Leases mechanism. How do master leases allow consistent linearizable reads without running Phase 2 accepts for read-only queries?
In the Raft protocol, explain why a candidate node that increments its term must explicitly persist currentTerm and votedFor to non-volatile disk before sending RequestVote.
Formulate the LWW-Element-Set (Last-Write-Wins Element Set) CRDT. What are its failure modes when distributed physical clocks experience NTP drift?
Explain the concept of Chain Replication in distributed storage. How does it separate read path at the tail and write path at the head to achieve high throughput?
Describe the Zab (ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast) protocol's recovery phase versus broadcast phase. How does it differ from Paxos in maintaining FIFO order?
Explain the concept of Quorum Leases in distributed caches. How do they balance read latency with cache invalidation guarantees across partitions?
Analyze how Byzantine Fault Tolerant protocols like Tendermint consensus utilize 2/3+1 voting rounds (Pre-vote and Pre-commit) to achieve instant finality.
In distributed systems, what is Chandy-Lamport distributed snapshotting algorithm? How do marker messages record global state without stopping execution?
Analyze the Raft log truncation scenario: explain what occurs when an elected leader detects a follower log mismatch at index N and decrements nextIndex.
Explain how the Groth16 zk-SNARK achieves 3-group-element proof size. Why is it non-malleable only under specific simulation-sound variants?
Detail the role of roots of unity in vanishing polynomial Z_H(X) = X^n - 1 over a multiplicative subgroup in polynomial SNARKs.
Explain how multi-scalar multiplication (MSM) dominates prover computation time in elliptic-curve SNARKs, and how Pippenger's algorithm optimizes it.
Explain the Reed-Solomon proximity testing problem in STARKs and how the FRI (Fast Reed-Solomon Interactive Oracle Proof) protocol solves it.
Describe the difference between arithmetic circuits over prime fields versus boolean circuits. Why do hashes like Poseidon or Rescue outperform SHA-256 in ZKPs?
Explain how look-up arguments (such as Plookup and Halo2 Lookups) bypass expensive R1CS multiplication gates for bitwise operations and ranges.
Detail how the Sumcheck protocol verifies that the sum of a multivariate polynomial over a Boolean hypercube equals a claimed scalar in O(d log N) verifier time.
Explain how Zero-Knowledge Rollups (ZK-Rollups) verify thousands of layer-2 transactions off-chain and commit succinct state roots to layer-1.
Explain the concept of DLOG hardness on elliptic curves and how it underpins the binding property of Pedersen commitments: C = g^m h^r.
Analyze the difference between interactive arguments and proofs. Why does statistical soundness differ from computational soundness in SNARKs?
Explain the 5-qubit quantum code [[5, 1, 3]]. Why is it the smallest possible code capable of protecting a logical qubit against arbitrary single-qubit errors?
Describe how X-cut and Z-cut topological boundary conditions in planar surface codes define logical operators X_L and Z_L on boundaries.
Explain how Lattice Surgery implements fault-tolerant logical CNOT gates between two planar surface code patches using merge and split operations.
Detail the role of the Clifford hierarchy P_k in quantum error correction. Why does the T gate sit at level 3, outside the Clifford group at level 2?
Explain how the Union-Find decoder works as an alternative to MWPM in surface codes, and why its O(N) complexity enables real-time syndrome decoding.
Describe how leakage errors (where qubits leave the |0>, |1> computational subspace) threaten fault-tolerant codes, and how Leakage Reduction Units (LRUs) reset them.
Explain the Bacon-Shor subsystem code. How do gauge operators simplify syndrome extraction compared to standard stabilizer codes?
What is the physical meaning of fault-tolerance threshold ~1% in surface codes under depolarizing noise models?
Explain how quantum teleportation of gates (Gottesman-Chuang trick) enables execution of non-Clifford gates using offline prepared magic states.
Analyze the difference between geometric locality in 2D surface codes versus high-rate LDPC (Low-Density Parity-Check) quantum codes.
Explain how Hamiltonian Neural Networks parameterize kinetic and potential energy T(p) and V(q) to learn physics from raw trajectory data.
Explain how Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) parameterize dynamics using L(q, q_dot) and the Euler-Lagrange equations without requiring canonical momenta.
Describe how adaptive step-size ODE solvers (such as Dormand-Prince / RK45) adjust step size Delta t based on local truncation error estimates during forward Neural ODE passes.
Explain how Augmented Neural ODEs resolve the limitation of standard Neural ODEs in learning trajectories with self-intersecting flows.
Explain the concept of Symplectic Matrix group Sp(2n, R) and why any Hamiltonian transformation must satisfy M^T J M = J.
Describe the role of Picard-Lindelof Theorem in ensuring unique solutions to Neural ODE initial value problems: dz/dt = f(z, t).
Explain how neural vector fields with non-zero curl fail to represent conservative forces in physical systems.
Explain how discrete residual connections z_{k+1} = z_k + f(z_k) approximate continuous Euler discretization of an underlying continuous neural flow.
Analyze why stiff differential equations cause extreme step size contraction in explicit Runge-Kutta solvers and require implicit A-stable methods.
Explain how spectral normalization restricts the Lipschitz constant of each linear layer W to ||W||_2 <= 1 to enforce globally contractive neural networks.
Explain how Functoriality preserves identities and composition: F(id_A) = id_{F(A)} and F(g o f) = F(g) o F(f). What happens if a mapping fails compositionality?
Explain the universal property of the Categorical Product A x B. How do projection morphisms pi_1 and pi_2 uniquely factor any pair of morphisms f: C -> A, g: C -> B?
Explain the universal property of the Categorical Coproduct A + B and its canonical inclusion morphisms i_1 and i_2.
Explain how the Reader Monad (-> R) and State Monad (s -> (a, s)) are formulated categorically as endofunctors with Kleisli triples.
Describe the difference between an Equivalence of Categories versus an Isomorphism of Categories. What role do natural isomorphisms of functors play?
Explain the concept of a Sheaf on a topological space and how the gluing axiom ensures local consistency leads to unique global sections.
Explain how an Epimorphism is defined categorically without referring to element surjectivity: g o f = h o f implies g = h.
Explain how a Monomorphism is defined categorically: f o g = f o h implies g = h, and why it models injective structure preservation.
Explain the adjunction between Free and Forgetful functors (Free -| Forgetful) using the example of Sets and Groups.
Explain how Dependent Type Theory formalizes Pi-types (dependent function types) and Sigma-types (dependent pair types) categorically as local cartesian closed categories.
